_why: ADR 0141's PYTHON half, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
The defect: `--s0 10mM` became NaN in the CLI, `null` in JSON, and was
then filtered out here -- so the document told a student 's0 is missing
-- yours to choose' about a number they had chosen. A refusal that
blames the user for the tool's own data loss is worse than a crash.
Split from the TypeScript half (adr-0141-cli-quantities.json) because a
set has ONE test command and this ADR's evidence spans two runners.
Chaining jest and pytest into one command would make the harness's test
counting read one runner's output as the other's.

mutations.description: a null value is dropped silently again
mutations._note: The original defect, restored. This is the line that turned a lost number into a lecture about not providing it.

The obvious guard, `if not entry.get('value')`, refuses a legitimate s0 of 0 -- the same class of bug as the one being fixed, a real number read as absence. Pinned so a later edit cannot reintroduce it.

mutations.description: the payload is checked only after the network call
mutations._note: Where this guard first sat. The observed failure was `Could not resolve 'km': 403 Forbidden` -- the network masking the payload defect entirely, and the check untestable without a network.
